rationale: Roberts is likely to keep the opinion narrow—FSIA’s civil-action structure does not divest § 3231 criminal jurisdiction—so he or Kagan are the most natural authors, with Gorsuch also plausible for a text/structure-focused opinion. Thomas is highly likely to write alone on clear-statement/sovereign-immunity grounds, and one or more concurrences (especially from Gorsuch/Barrett/Alito) may emphasize that any residual immunity is a common-law merits defense rather than a jurisdictional bar.
